findings.description: The recorded division-folding probe result '0/262144 bit differences for every divisor (3.0, 7.0, 0.1, pi, 1e6, 9.7)' in fastmath_contraction_audit.json and llvm_ir_division.txt is not reproducible. Reviewer measures 39656/262144 (~15.1%) differing standard-normal f32 values for the pi divisor alone, and 30/64 differing linspace values comparing drjit literal-divisor vs data-divisor paths for d=3.0 with FastMath OFF. The qualitative hazard claim (Dr.Jit folds literal divisors into host reciprocal multiplies even with FastMath off; IR inspection is the reliable detector) is CORRECT and was independently confirmed; only the recorded number is wrong, and the error is in the conservative direction (the hazard is easier to detect by value than recorded, which strengthens rather than weakens the case for the structural mitigation).
findings.recommendation: Author amends the probe sentence in evidence/llvm_ir_division.txt and evidence/fastmath_contraction_audit.json (and proof_record.md) to the reproduced rates; affected scope for re-review is only the division-hazard note, not the kernel.

findings.description: fastmath_contraction_audit.json describes its dump as 'one full symbolic-kernel launch' but the file records two kernel launches per call (a side-effect mask-scatter loop kernel plus the main compute kernel); the audit counts (e.g. 27 masked.gather) span both kernels. The no-contraction conclusion is unchanged (reviewer recounted across both kernels and across a fresh dump).
findings.recommendation: Wording fix in the audit JSON; optionally note the two-launch structure since it matters for per-call launch-overhead accounting in trials.

findings.description: Trial-design: candidate thread usage is two pools - the drjit pool (dr.set_thread_count, process-global, count includes the calling thread) for JIT kernel execution, plus a separate per-call host ThreadPoolExecutor(min(8, cpu_count)) used only for large-B transposes inside the adapter. The numba baseline uses a single pool. Under the B7-03 equal-CPU-budget rule these are different budget shapes and must be labeled as such; B7-03 process isolation already prevents the process-global drjit state (FastMath off, thread count) from leaking between configurations.
findings.recommendation: In B7-31, pin dr.set_thread_count to the same CPU budget as the numba pool for the paired comparison, report the transpose-pool width alongside, and log requested/configured/effective counts after init per protocol.

findings.description: Trial-design: cold-first-use measurement depends on DRJIT_CACHE_DIR state - compiled LLVM kernels persist on disk across processes (author records 150.6 ms uncached vs 4.7 ms warm). The B7-03 cold-first-use guard must freeze the cache regime explicitly. Adapter stage costs (pack/validate/transposes ~20 ms at B=65536, symbolic run ~49 ms, materialize ~0.3 ms) exist only in proof_record prose, not in the timing evidence JSON.
findings.recommendation: Freeze DRJIT_CACHE_DIR (empty vs pre-warmed) as part of the trial freeze; measure and record adapter stage costs in the trial evidence JSONs.

findings.description: Dev-tier timing JSON lacks a recorded LLVM version fingerprint (only 'Dr.Jit LLVM JIT' and apple-m1 target features); B7-03 runtime_fingerprints asks for llvm version per trial. Also B=96 pair showed high variance (C: 1.046 vs 2.646 ms) - acceptable for dev-tier, must be handled by the B7-03 paired-median design.
findings.recommendation: Record the LLVM version string in the capability token / trial fingerprints.
